data.narrative:
Vertical Aerospace is a public-stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector that has raised $50M to date. The valuation universe for this company consists of eight private peers within Drones & Autonomous, including Joby Aviation, Archer Aviation, Waymo, Wayve, and Zipline. There are no public comparables in the narrowly defined peer set, limiting the availability of direct market-based benchmarks.

The peer-median triangulation method is not applicable to this valuation. The Drones & Autonomous sector contains seven same-sector peers overall, but the analysis identified only two companies at the same stage and zero peers in adjacent stages or similar valuation tiers. This fails the minimum threshold of three datapoints required for a defensible peer-median approach. Reliance on all-sector medians would introduce excessive heterogeneity and render the analysis unreliable given the distinct characteristics of players across the broader autonomous vehicles and drone markets.

Without sufficient narrow peer coverage, traditional comparable company methods cannot be reliably applied. A complete valuation would require supplementary approaches such as precedent transaction analysis within the sector, discounted cash flow modeling if forward financials are available, or venture capital method frameworks calibrated to the stage and capital requirements of frontier autonomous technology companies. Key uncertainties include the path to profitability, regulatory approval timelines, and the capital intensity required to scale hardware-based autonomous platforms.
